title: Inference ecosystem usage and competitive synthesis for procurement-trigger heuristics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: produce a compact, operational competitive synthesis that maps market model supply signals to Redwood procurement triggers and product guardrails. This ticket scopes the PM-side research, deliverables, and acceptance criteria for a 3-part output: 1) competitor archetype matrix with signal-to-action mappings; 2) a prioritized signal telemetry spec (events/thresholds + sampling cadence); 3) a lightweight prototype dashboard and alert recipe for Sales/Procurement to surface at-risk workloads.

Why now: customers increasingly ask for guidance on fallback economics and procurement timing. We need a repeatable way to translate model-landscape telemetry (availability, latency spikes, quantization coverage, regional capacity) into product and Sales signals (offer dedicated capacity, propose quantized variants, trigger procurement outreach).

Scope / Inclusions:
- Competitive sweep across 6 representative providers (open and managed) focusing on availability SLAs, release cadence, quantization support, and regional presence.
- Field interviews: 6 customer-facing interviews (solutions, sales, 2 Enterprise customers) to capture procurement triggers and tolerance thresholds.
- Telemetry mapping: list of events and aggregated metrics that can be implemented in Console (e.g., weekly capacity failures by region; 95th pctl latency delta vs baseline; sudden model variant deprecation).
- Decision rules: draft heuristics for when to surface specific product interventions (e.g., recommend Dedicated capacity, auto-fallback to quantized variant, initiate account outreach).
- Prototype: single-page dashboard (Data Studio / internal Console mock) and two alert recipes for Ops and Sales.

Out of scope: deep legal/license negotiation drafts, implementation work for Dedicated autoscale changes, or full infra instrumentation (this ticket hands off a telemetry spec).

Deliverables:
- One-page Competitor Archetype Matrix (PDF + Confluence) with recommended vendor action(s).
- Telemetry Spec (CSV table) with sampling cadence and alert thresholds.
- Prototype dashboard link + two alert recipe scripts for Sales/Procurement to instrument.
- Runbook outline that maps alerts to next steps and owner (Sales, Solutions, Platform Ops).

Success metrics:
- Internal acceptance by Sales and Procurement leadership (email signoff).
- Prototype dashboard validated with at least 2 field reps and 1 pilot account.
- Actionability: for >=3 common customer workflows we can map a telemetry pattern to a prescriptive product/sales action within 24 hours.

Stakeholders: Sofia (PM owner), Riley Park (Sales lead), Marcus Osei (Solutions), Priya Rao (Platform Ops), Design review by Des team.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Chen: Kickoff complete. Initial competitor list: OpenModelA, OpenModelB (quant builds), ProviderX managed endpoints, ProviderY regional edge, VerticaAI (specialty), CloudCo managed. Confirmed SOW with Sales to schedule 4 field interviews.

2025-02-26 - Riley Park: Sales feedback: need alert recipes that translate to 'Customer likely to request SLA' and 'Customer candidate for Dedicated' — include recommended offer text and cost delta estimate to speed follow-up.

2025-03-04 - Design review (Des team): requested simplified color rules and call-to-action buttons on dashboard; supplied two copy variants for Sales outreach. Updated prototype mock in Drive.

2025-03-05 - Sofia Martinez: Iteration plan: finalize telemetry spec this week, runbook draft by 2025-03-12, then handoff to Platform Ops and Dedicated team for pilot instrumentation.
